title: OneDrive sync will skip new node_modules folders by default
summary: From 14 December 2026, the OneDrive sync app for Windows and Mac will stop syncing newly created folders named node_modules (any capitalisation), according to Message Center MC1558030 (read via a third-party mirror). Existing node_modules folders keep syncing and nothing is deleted; users get no prompt, and the folders stay local only. It extends the default exclusion list that already covers .db-wal files, and admins can switch the default exclusions off with existing OneDrive sync policies. Rollout should finish by mid-January 2027.
why: Developers with projects in Known Folder Move locations (Desktop, Documents) will suddenly find dependencies missing on a second device or in the web. If your backup or restore story relies on OneDrive for those folders, the restore will be incomplete by design.
todo: Do now: tell developers and the service desk that node_modules will be local-only and should be rebuilt with the package manager, not restored from OneDrive.
If you need these folders synced, set the OneDrive policy that disables the default exclusion list before 14 December 2026.
Use the change to move code projects out of KFM folders into a Git-backed location instead.
Wait: no action needed if the new default suits you.
effective_note: Rollout 14 Dec 2026 to mid-January 2027 — per MC1558030 (third-party mirror).
